title: Confucianism and Its Rivals
altTitles: The Story of Confucianism and Its Rivals
author: herbert-giles
attributionNote: Eight lectures by Herbert Allen Giles (1845–1935), the Cambridge sinologist who also translated the Zhuangzi, the Liezi and much of Chinese literature.
description: Confucianism and Its Rivals tells the history of Chinese religion in eight lectures, from the earliest times to 1915: the rise of Confucianism, the challenge of the Taoists and the Buddhists, the fortunes of the literati under Buddhist and Mongol rule, and the state cult of Confucius in the last imperial centuries. Giles writes as a historian of institutions and beliefs rather than as a theologian.
historicalContext: The lectures were delivered at the Lowell Institute in Boston and published in London in 1915, a decade before the examination system's Confucian curriculum was dismantled. They record how a nineteenth-century sinologist read the tradition's rivals, and where his judgments have dated.
availabilityNote: Complete: the eight lectures, streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one lecture per chapter. The author's preface is not part of the work.
